# Wisdom of Solomon Chapter 10 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Wisdom 10 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/WIS_010_page_001.jpg

---

**1** She guarded the first-formed father of the world, who had been created alone, and she rescued him from his own transgression,

**2** and gave him strength to rule over all things.

**3** But when an unrighteous man departed from her in anger, he perished in the fratricidal rage that he himself had kindled.

**4** When because of him the earth was flooded, Wisdom again rescued it, steering the righteous man through worthless timber.

**5** She also — when the nations were being confounded in their wicked compact — recognized the righteous man and kept him blameless before God, and kept him resolute in the face of compassion for his child.

**6** When the ungodly were perishing, Wisdom rescued a righteous man who fled from the fire descending on the Five Cities.

**7** Of their wickedness there stands witness to this day: a region of desolation still smoking, plants bearing fruit that does not ripen in season, and a pillar of salt standing there — a monument to a soul that did not believe.

**8** For, having passed Wisdom by, not only were they harmed by failing to know the good, but they also left for the living a memorial of their folly, so that their stumbling could not pass unnoticed.

**9** But Wisdom rescued from troubles those who served her.

**10** She guided through straight paths a righteous man who was fleeing from a brother's wrath; she showed him the kingdom of God and gave him knowledge of holy things; she prospered him in his labors and multiplied the fruit of his toil.

**11** When in their greed those who oppressed him stood against him, she stood by him and made him rich.

**12** She guarded him from his enemies and kept him safe from those who lay in wait; she judged for him a hard contest, so that he might know that godliness is mightier than all.

**13** She did not forsake a righteous man when he was sold, but delivered him from sin;

**14** she went down with him into a pit, and in chains she did not abandon him, until she brought him the scepter of a kingdom and authority over those who had lorded it over him; she proved false those who had accused him and gave him eternal glory.

**15** She rescued a holy people and a blameless seed from a nation of oppressors.

**16** She entered into the soul of a servant of the Lord and withstood fearsome kings by wonders and signs.

**17** She gave the holy ones the reward of their labors; she led them on a marvelous road and became for them a shelter by day and a flame of stars by night.

**18** She brought them across the Red Sea and led them through deep waters.

**19** But their enemies she overwhelmed, and from the depth of the abyss she cast them up.

**20** Therefore the righteous plundered the ungodly, and they sang praises, O Lord, to your holy name and extolled with one accord your defending hand,

**21** because Wisdom opened the mouths of the mute and made the tongues of infants speak plainly.
